review_notes: Read the whole file and the Mathlib homologyIsCokernel API. Two repeated-proof patterns are reported: the cokernel-descent construction (used twice) and the four bilinearity obligations in cupZ. The `have := congrArg (fun φ => φ.hom _)` unwrapping idiom appears in five places, but each use is a short routine unfolding, so I didn't report it separately. The rewritten code is untested, and the exact simp/rw steps in the proposed lemmas may need adjustment.

findings.declaration: cupZH / π_cupZH / cupHH / π_cupHH (with cond_right, cond_left)
findings.problem: The same descent construction is written out twice. Each time, a map out of cocycles that kills boundaries is lifted through `homologyIsCokernel` using `CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc'`. The `π_*` lemma is then proved by re-stating the whole `desc'` term inside `congrArg`, followed by the same `simp only [ModuleCat.hom_comp, LinearMap.comp_apply, Limits.Cofork.π_ofπ] at this; exact this`. The only differences are the complex (A or B), the degree, and the map. This pairs `cupZH` with `cupHH` and `π_cupZH` with `π_cupHH`, and the long `desc'` expressions have to be kept in sync by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Add one general helper, stated for any `A : Rep k G`, degree `n` and `M : ModuleCat k`. `descH A n (f : cocycles A n ⟶ M) (hf : toCocycles A ((ComplexShape.up ℕ).prev n) n ≫ f = 0) : groupCohomology A n ⟶ M := (Limits.CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc' ((inhomogeneousCochains A).homologyIsCokernel _ n rfl) f hf).1`. Add its companion `descH_π (z : cocycles A n) : (descH A n f hf).hom ((groupCohomology.π A n).hom z) = f.hom z`. The proof of `descH_π` is the existing `congrArg … .2` followed by `simp only [...]` block, written once. Then `cupZH := descH B q (ModuleCat.ofHom (cupZ A B p q x)) (cond_right A B p q x)` and `cupHH := descH A p (ModuleCat.ofHom (cupZHlin A B p q)) (cond_left A B p q)`. Likewise `π_cupZH` and `π_cupHH` become one-line applications of `descH_π`, closed by `rfl` or `simpa` where needed. Check that the `cond_*` hypotheses match the `prev` form required by `hf`.
findings.benefit: The cokernel-descent argument and its `Cofork.π_ofπ` simp unwinding appear once instead of twice, and the two `π_*` lemmas shrink to one-line corollaries. A reader can see that both cup constructions are instances of one universal property. A change in the Mathlib API (e.g. `desc'` or `homologyIsCokernel`) needs one fix instead of two.

evidence.excerpt: simp only [ModuleCat.hom_comp, LinearMap.comp_apply, Limits.Cofork.π_ofπ] at this
noncomputable def homologyIsCokernel (hi : c.prev j = i) [K.HasHomology j]

findings.problem: The four `mk₂` obligations (additivity and homogeneity in each variable) repeat one argument. Each one `show`s the goal with the long `(groupCohomology.π (A ⊗ B) (p + q)).hom (zcup …)` expression, rewrites with `← map_add` or `← map_smul`, and applies `congrArg _ (iCocycles_injective _ _ …)`. It then checks equality of the underlying cochains by `rw [..., i_zcup, ...]; simp only [...]`. The real mathematical content is that `zcup` is bilinear, which is proved by injectivity of `iCocycles` and bilinearity of `cochainCup`. That content is mixed in with four copies of the π-wrapping boilerplate.
findings.proposed_change: First prove bilinearity of `zcup` separately: `zcup_add_left`, `zcup_smul_left`, `zcup_add_right`, `zcup_smul_right`. Each is `apply iCocycles_injective; rw [map_add (or map_smul), i_zcup, i_zcup, i_zcup]; simp only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply]` (or the smul analogue), which is the inner `by` block that is already there. Alternatively, build `zcup` as a bilinear map by `LinearMap.mk₂` and compose it with `π`. The `cupZ` obligations then reduce to `by simp only [zcup_add_left, map_add]`, `by simp only [zcup_smul_left, map_smul]`, and the two right-variable analogues, with no `show` blocks. If a single helper is preferred, state it as: for `f : cocycles (A⊗B) n →ₗ M`, `f (zcup … (x+x') y) = …`.
findings.benefit: The bilinearity of the cocycle-level cup product becomes a set of named, reusable lemmas that are also usable elsewhere (e.g. in `cupZ_right_boundary`). The definition of `cupZ` becomes short and readable, and the four sets of repeated `show` statements disappear.

evidence.excerpt: rw [map_add, i_zcup, i_zcup, i_zcup]; simp only [map_add, LinearMap.add_apply])))
